# PR #3522: Patch: a dungeon run shows your deck, relics, blessings, curses and seed between fights, and a past run's curses by name

Closes #3501

## What changed

The dungeon HUD now has a **Your run** button on every screen the run screen draws, run-over included. A fight draws `FightScreen`, so it has none. The button opens the shared `Dialog` with:

- the **seed** (first, so a 40-card deck can't push it off a phone) and a **Copy seed** button;
- the **deck** as a compact grid of `RunCardFace`s, which already draw the Radiant face and the "Buffs: n" line;
- the **relics** with level and text, the **blessings** with text, and the **curses** with name, points and text. Each list says "No …" when empty.

`RunOverScreen` shows "Seed: …". `DungeonStats` names a record's curses from the run content, and an id the content lacks shows as the id.

- **New:** `RunPanel.tsx` and `run-panel.css` (design tokens only, no `@media`, no `max-height` because the scrim scrolls the panel).
- **Display and ids:** `RunDisplay.tsx` gains `curseName` and `CurseChoice`; `testids.ts` gains the panel and seed ids.
- **Store:** `store.ts` exports the existing `contentOf`.
- **Strings:** four keys in `zh-CN.json` ("Your run", "Blessings", "No blessings", "Copy seed"). Every other string reuses an existing key.
- **Docs:** one paragraph each in spec §15.5 and §15.10, and the Dialog users' list in `apps/web/README.md`.
- **Not touched:** no Rust, `wire/`, `fight/` or bot paths. No ruling was needed.

## Tests

- `RunScreen.test.tsx`, new `#3501` block (9 tests):
  - the panel lists every deck card with its Radiant and Buffs marks, each relic, blessing and curse with its text, and the seed;
  - the empty states, with an unknown curse id falling back to the id;
  - an empty deck draws the note, not an empty grid;
  - the ✕ takes focus, Escape and ✕ close it, and focus returns to the button;
  - Copy seed writes "ABCDEF" and shows "Copied";
  - a refused clipboard leaves "Copy seed";
  - the button is on the run-over screen;
  - the run-over screen shows "Seed: QWERTY";
  - the phone-width layout, checked against the sheet's rules.
- `DungeonStats.test.tsx`: a record's curses show by name, and an unknown id shows as itself. The store mock gains `contentOf`.

Commands I ran, all green:

- `pnpm --dir apps/web test src/dungeon/map/RunScreen.test.tsx src/dungeon/stats/DungeonStats.test.tsx`: 37 passed.
- `pnpm --dir apps/web test src/i18n/i18n.test.ts src/writing.test.ts src/wording.test.ts src/spacing.test.ts src/typescale.test.ts src/surfaces.test.ts src/palette.test.ts src/buttons.test.ts src/dialogs.test.ts src/breakpoints.test.ts src/dungeon`: 21 files, 183 tests passed.
- `pnpm --dir apps/web typecheck` and `pnpm exec eslint apps/web/src/dungeon`: no output.
- `cargo jackioh spec check`: ok.
- `pnpm exec vitest run --project web --changed origin/main` with the harness's excludes: 342 files, 6739 passed, 109 skipped.

`cargo fmt --check` and the Rust checks were not run, because no Rust changed. I did not boot the client at 360 px. jsdom can't lay it out, so the phone-width acceptance item is covered only by the CSS test.

## Departures from the plan

- `RunPanel` has a small local `PassiveList` component for the relic, blessing and curse lists, instead of three copies of the same markup. The DOM and test ids are as the plan gives them.
- I added a test for the empty deck.
- The header comment of `DungeonStats.tsx` said it never reads the engine. I amended it to say it also reads the compiled-in run content, which is public, to name curses.

## Decisions the issue did not settle

- **Fight tray:** the issue's "Why" says curses never show in a fight, but its proposal doesn't touch the tray. I left `fight/` unchanged. The alternative was adding curses to the tray, which a person may want later.
- **Seed first in the panel:** the issue lists it last. I put it first so a long deck can't push it out of view on a phone.
- **Curse names on the stats page:** they come from the current compiled content, not the content the run was played on, because a record stores only ids. A dropped id shows as the id.

- The panel's Dialog renders as a child of the HUD `<header>`. It is `position: fixed`, so it covers the window, as `DungeonStats`'s dialog does inside the tavern shell.
